warmup.description: Gently activate full body with emphasis on coordination and joint control.
movements: Marching in place with arm swings x 60s

main_exercises.name: Single-Leg Sit-to-Stand (assisted if needed)
main_exercises.load_guidance: Bodyweight only, use support as needed for balance
main_exercises.form_cue: Control the descent and keep knee aligned over toes

main_exercises.name: Bird Dog (with pause)
main_exercises.load_guidance: Bodyweight only, focus on slow and controlled movement
main_exercises.form_cue: Pause at full extension and keep hips level

main_exercises.name: Lateral Step and Reach
main_exercises.load_guidance: Bodyweight only, focus on coordination and control
main_exercises.form_cue: Step softly and reach across the body with control

main_exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Anti-Rotation Hold (Band)
main_exercises.load_guidance: Light resistance band, prioritize stability over tension
main_exercises.form_cue: Keep torso upright and resist rotation through the core

main_exercises.name: Heel-to-Toe Balance Walk
main_exercises.form_cue: Place each foot directly in front of the other and stay tall

cooldown.description: Calm the body and reinforce mobility with gentle stretching and breath.
movements: Seated spinal twist x 30s each side

phase_notes.menstrual: This low-intensity, coordination-focused session is ideal—move slowly and prioritize balance and comfort over precision.
phase_notes.follicular: Great time to refine coordination—focus on smoother, more controlled transitions and improved balance.
phase_notes.ovulatory: You may feel more stable and coordinated—use this to improve control and confidence in movement patterns.
phase_notes.early_luteal: Maintain consistency and focus on clean, controlled movement—this session supports stability without fatigue.
phase_notes.late_luteal: Keep movements slow and grounded—this session can help maintain coordination while reducing stress and fatigue.
